LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To talk about things you can see in different places 
in the world and things you can buy or do in a shop.
•	 To understand obligation, lack of obligation and advice.
MATERIALS
•	 TR#9 Prepositions Actions Song
•	 TR#18 Genie in a Bottle Song
•	 TR#20 Time to Go Home
•	 Calendar (P.E.M.1)
•	 After-School Activities (P.E.M.2) 
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 4: Country flash cards (P.4.3)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 2: sets of Memory cards 
(P.4.2 + P.4.7)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 6: Country memory cards 
(P.4.2) + Attraction cards (P.4.7)
•	 Big Book  
•	 Magic Creature and Places (A3) and Magic Creature 
and Country cards (P.S4)
•	 Crayons or pencils 
•	 Day 3 stickers (1 per child)
BEFORE CLASS
Check the teacher’s dashboard to see if the Ss have completed 
at least half of the recommended activities up to this point.
LESSON PLAN
1.– WARM-UP ROUTINES (9’) 
•	 Hello + register + booklets 
•	 Calendar
•	 After-School Activities
2.– STORY WITH CHANGES (PP.2-8) (10’)
Have your students choose the storytelling variables and 
tell them the first half of the story. Please see the section on 
storytelling in the Warm-Up Routines Index.

3.– ACTIVITY 4: WHERE ARE YOU FROM? (5’)
P.4.3
Italy
> How to Play
Ss must ask and answer questions about where they and their 
classmates are from according to the flash cards they pick up.
> Warm-Up
First, model the activity. Choose a Country flash card (P.4.3) 
and ask the Ss, “Can you guess where I’m from?”. Say for 
example, “Where I’m from, you can see Big Ben, people speak 
English, and it’s always rainy.”. The Ss must guess by asking, 
“Are you from England?” and then, you must respond by saying 
either “Yes, I am.” or “No, I am not.”
> Main Activity
A Ss chooses a Country flash card (P.4.3) and keeps it a secret 
from the rest. The group then asks, “Where are you from?”. 
The S should give clues using the following structures:
•	 Where I’m from people speak…
•	 Where I’m from you can see…
•	 Where I’m from people eat…
•	 Where I’m from you can visit…
Ss must guess their classmate’s country by asking for 
example, “Are you from Australia?” to which the S should 
reply, “Yes, I am,” or “No, I am not.” Make sure that every S 
participates either by taking a country or by asking questions. 
As it can take a long time for all Ss to have a go at this activity 
we recommend that you take a note of any Ss that didn’t get 
a go so they can go first the following day.
> Follow-Up
Ask Ss quick questions about the country they are from. 
Say, “What language do people speak where you are from?”, 
“What can you see there?”, “What do people eat?”, “What can 
you visit?”. Let the group come up with ideas and respond by 
saying: “Where I’m from…”

4.– WORKSHEET: WHERE DID THEY GO? (P.6) (8’)
Where Did They Go?
Australia
South Africa
United States of 
America
India
Egypt
China
6
MATERIALS
•	 crayons or pencils
NOTE: if you collected your Ss’ books during the booklet 
activity, have them ask you for it now by saying, “Can I have 
my book please?”; otherwise, ask them to take it out of their 
bag. Explain the activity before giving out the books/asking Ss 
to take them out since they might get distracted.
TARGET LANGUAGE
Grandma went to India to visit her family.
Grandma went to the United States of America to visit 
the Statue of Liberty.
Grandma went to South Africa to see the elephants.
Grandma, Pam and Paul went to Australia to see the 
kangaroos.
Pam and Paul went to Egypt to visit the pyramids.
Pam and Paul went to China to visit the Great Wall.
This worksheet is divided into three columns: Pam and Paul, 
and Grandma, on the left; countries they visited in the middle; 
and on the right, what they saw and visited in each country.
Ss must match the characters with the correct destinations 
and attractions. While pointing to a country, ask the Ss, “Who 
went to Australia?” to which they should respond, “Grandma, 
Pam and Paul went to Australia,”. Continue by asking, “What 
did they see there?” and let the Ss respond, “They saw the 
kangaroos.” Then have the Ss draw lines to connect the 
characters to the correct places and things that can be seen 
there. Continue in this manner until the worksheet is complete. 
To review, ask the children incorrect questions like, “Did Paul 
go to America?” and have them correct you saying, “No, he 
didn’t. Grandma went to America.”

> Advanced Students
If your group already understands the structures and knows 
how to say them, encourage them to ask these questions 
during the activity. At the end of the activity, they can ask their 
classmates the incorrect questions.

> Scenario A
If your group has achieved the activity goal on My Way (i.e., 
they have done all or most of the activities in the current Mission), 
say, “You’re doing amazing on My Way! You have played lots 
of games in Mission 4, so we can do a special sticker activity 
together!”. Take the Day 3 stickers and have them ask, “Can I 
have some stickers, please?”. Do the activity as instructed below. 
> Scenario B
If your group hasn’t reached the activity goal on My Way, 
simply move on with the class. You will have to complete one 
or two activities from the bonus section to make up for the 
time allotted to this dynamic.

The point of this activity is to review talking about nationalities 
in a fun way. Ss have to stick the stickers and answer the 
questions by looking at the characters and the visual clues 
in the centre of the spread. Model the task by looking for the 
stickers, sticking them, and answering the questions.
Have Ss open pp.20-21 (sticker section) and say, “Let’s find 
out where these people are from!”. Point to rectangle number 
51 and ask, “What number is this?”. Ss should respond, “It’s 
number 51!”. Say, “Can you find number 51 on the sticker sheet? 
Which country is it?”, and elicit, “Here it is! It’s South Africa.”. 
Then say, “Who is from South Africa? Character number 4, 8, 
or 9?” (point to the corresponding character). The Ss should 
answer, “Character 4 (Nora) is from South Africa!”
Follow the same procedure for stickers 52-58 and do as many 
as time allows. 
We recommend making this activity more dynamic by turning 
it into a competition to answer the questions as fast as possible. 
You can give points to Ss who respond correctly.
If you can’t finish the whole activity, tell the Ss that they can 
continue at home.
KEY
Sticker 51: Who is from South Africa? Number 4 (Nora) 
is from South Africa. 
Sticker 52: Who is from the United States of America? 
Number 6 (Jason) is from the United States of America.
Sticker 53: Who is from China? Number 2 (Mei) is from 
China.
Sticker 54: Who is from Egypt? Number 12 (Lana) is from 
Egypt.
Sticker 55: Who is from Canada? Number 3 (Dave) is 
from Canada.
Sticker 56: Who is from France? Number 8 (Nancy) is 
from France.
Sticker 57: Who is from Germany? Number 10 (Hans) is 
from Germany.
Sticker 58: Who is from Italy? Number 1 (Mark) is from Italy.
NOTE: Ss might not remember the names of the characters 
from Story 3. You can either help them recall or simply refer to 
the characters with the numbers. It’s the first time characters 
2 and 10 appear.

7.– ACTIVITY 6: TRAVEL TIPS (7’)
P.4.2
England
P.4.7
> How to Play
Ss should find matching pairs of countries (P.4.2) and the 
things that they can see or visit there (P.4.7). When they get a 
correct match, Ss must give advice on what to do there.
> Warm-Up
Take a country card (P.4.2) at random and say “I’m going to 
Japan. What should I visit?” to which Ss should reply, “If you 
go to Japan, you should visit Mount Fuji.” Try to quickly review 
at least five more countries.
> Main Activity
Before class, prepare decks consisting of six cards: three 
countries, and three things you can do there (one per country). 
You will need as many decks as pairs of Ss in your group.
Put the Ss into pairs. Deal S1 the country cards and S2 the 
activity cards. S1 takes a country card and says for example, 
“I’m going to Italy. What should I visit?”. Then S2 looks for the 
corresponding card in their deck, shows it to their partner and 
says, “If you go to Italy, you should visit the Leaning Tower 
of Pisa.” Give each S at least two pairs to work on.
If time allows, redistribute the different decks and change 
their roles (from asking for advice to giving it, and vice versa).
> Follow-Up
Take two cards that don’t match and say for example, “If 
you go to Canada, you should visit the Eiffel Tower.”. Ss will 
see that it is not correct so encourage them to correct you by 
saying, “No, that’s wrong. If you go to Canada, you should 
see polar bears.”
NOTE: accept other options that the Ss might come up with, 
if they are correct and they use the proper structure.

8.– ACTIVITY 2: WHERE DID THEY GO? (8’)
P.4.2
P.4.2
Egypt
P.4.7
> How to Play
In this activity Ss will create sentences about the characters 
going to different countries and visiting different monuments.
> Warm-Up
Prepare three piles of cards face down, one with characters 
(P.4.2), one with countries (P.4.2) and the other with monuments, 
animals and food (P.4.7). Introduce the activity by saying, “Let’s 
find out where the characters travelled to last year!”. Model the 
activity for the Ss by drawing a card from each pile. If possible, 
model both a correct and an incorrect combination of cards.
For example:
•	 Take Pam, Egypt and Mount Fuji from each pile, and 
say, “Pam didn’t go to Egypt to visit Mount Fuji; she 
went to Japan to visit Mount Fuji.”
•	 Take Pam, Egypt and the Pyramids, and say, “Pam 
went to Egypt to visit the pyramids.”
> Main Activity
Ss take a card from each pile and identify whether the 
character went to the right country to visit the monument.
If, for example, they take Dad, India and Taj Mahal, they should 
form a sentence using the following structure: “Dad went to 
India to visit the Taj Mahal.” 
If they don’t find a match, they will have to state the correct 
activity for that country. For example, if a S takes Mum, South 
Africa and Taj Mahal, they will say, “Mum didn’t go to South 
Africa to visit the Taj Mahal; she went to South Africa to see 
the elephants.”
You can use prompts and actions where necessary if the Ss 
are unable to remember the different countries and monuments.

NOTE: to play this activity, it is not necessary to consider 
the actual places that the characters visited in the story. For 
cards with food items, you should change the target language 
accordingly “Mum didn’t go to China to eat curry, Mum went 
to India to eat curry.”. Same goes for “go on a safari”, “have a 
barbecue”, “eat noodles”, etc.
> Follow-Up
Once every S has had a turn, take a correct combination of 
cards and ask the Ss, “Where did Grandma go to and what did 
she do there?” to which the Ss should reply, “Grandma went 
to India to visit the Taj Mahal.”
Then, show an incorrect combination and ask, “Did Grandma 
go to South Africa to visit the Taj Mahal?” to which Ss should 
reply, “No, she didn’t. She went to India to visit the Taj Mahal.”

BONUS
PREPOSITIONS ACTION SONG (TR#9)
> Main Activity
Play the Prepositions Actions Song (TR#9) and dance to it. 
PREPOSITIONS ACTIONS SONG
(as you sing, simply perform the actions mentioned in the song. 
You can also create a hand choreography for the preposition 
verses.) 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
March in line, in, in line. 
(musical interlude)
Hide under the table, under, under the table.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Walk next to a friend, next to, next to a friend. 
(musical interlude)
Stand between two chairs, between, between two chairs.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Jump behind the teacher, behind, behind the teacher. 
(musical interlude)
Run in front of the board, in front of, in front of the board.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Sit on a chair, on, on a chair. 
(musical interlude)
This is the end, the end, the end.

ACTIVITY 5: RIGHT OR WRONG?
> How to Play
Show the Ss different pages from the Big Book and say a 
sentence about them. The Ss then have to decide if it is right 
or wrong.
> Main Activity
Introduce the activity by saying, “Let’s see how well you 
remember the story.”. Divide the Ss into two teams. Show the 
Ss different pages from the Big Book and say a right or wrong 
statement. For example, “Pam, Paul and Grandpa are cleaning 
the attic. Is that right or wrong?”. The Ss should respond, 
“That’s wrong!” and then correct it by saying “Pam, Paul and 
Grandma are cleaning the attic.” The Ss can decide together as 
a group whether the phrase is true or false, but they must take 
turns to reply. Every time one of the teams answers correctly, 
they get a point.
